rationale: Reconnaissance by information elicitation is coherent, but the stated data-versus-code boundary conflicts with credential-capture Initial Access in FT016/FT018; purpose needs to govern mapping. Visibility limitation is candid.
Victim-owned website is the source-specific collection behavior; later resource and access actions are explicitly consequences. Detection appropriately acknowledges external visibility limits.

Searching already leaked credential sets differs from scanning exposed files and subsequent credential use. Breach monitoring observes exposure rather than the adversary search; routine password rotation advice needs correction.

Organizational attributes are coherent Reconnaissance targets; linked identity attributes overlap but organizational relationships and tempo distinguish this parent. Detection admits limited visibility.
Business relationship discovery fits FT004 semantically; dependency exploitation is later use. Declared FT0004 is invalid and already dispositioned.
Physical-location collection fits organization-information discovery, distinct from exploiting premises. Invalid declared parent already recorded; passive detection limit appropriate.
Operational tempo is a distinct information target; later timed attacks are consequences. Invalid declared parent already recorded; passive collection visibility is limited.
Role and entitlement discovery is more specific than employee names alone. Semantically fits FT004 despite invalid parent; public collection visibility limitation is reasonable.
Victim identity collection is coherent Reconnaissance. Children partition credentials, emails and names; overlaps with payment-information collection require objective-based mapping.

Credentials are the information object; leaks, purchases and phishing are acquisition routes and takeover is follow-on. Reconnaissance plausible; scope crosses cookie theft/MFA service compromise, so collection routes are not synonyms.
Email-address discovery fits the parent; enumeration is an active route and public directories passive. Detection appropriately avoids claiming enterprise observation of all searches.
Names alone differ from roles and privileges. Fits identity parent and Reconnaissance; passive collection caveat adequate.
Automated exposed-secret search is coherent; credential use is a separate follow-on. Exposure scanners provide practical defender evidence, although they do not prove adversary scanning.
GitHub repository/history search fits FT006; secret prevention and exposure monitoring complement later API misuse signals. Blank parent is a known structural defect.

Description mixes exposed-file discovery with active password guessing and authentication bypass; these exceed parent secret-exposure scanning. Detection follows brute force and misses a clean collection boundary.

Telegram message searching fits credential collection but compromised-account history is post-access. Detection assumes access to channels/messages; ownership and monitoring visibility require qualification.

Parent defines unauthorized infiltration while children also rent, buy and establish resources. Resource Development works only with preparation-for-another-target boundary, not all direct victim intrusion.
Botnet acquisition/building is preparatory; credential stuffing and DDoS are downstream uses. Traffic detects use rather than procurement. Parent mismatch is already recorded.

DNS takeover and cache poisoning are distinct mechanisms mixed here; victim redirection dominates rather than infrastructure procurement. DNSSEC protects authenticated resolution, not arbitrary authorized-management changes.
Malvertising delivery is coherent but Resource Development should isolate ad procurement; detection is DNS-hijacking text and does not describe malicious ads or browser execution.

Direct intrusion into financial servers is conflated with preparation of attack resources. Owner-side authentication, integrity and network evidence are plausible; intended victim/resource boundary needs decision.

Edited scope is unauthorized control of existing VPS; excludes paid provisioning as defining mechanism. Provider/owner logs distinguished from financial-institution downstream signals. Existing parent mismatch remains.
VPN procurement/compromise as a resource is coherent; VPN-origin requests prove use, not theft or fraudulent acquisition. Detection needs explicit legitimate-use and provider-visibility limits.
Edited scope is stolen-payment rental/provisioning; takeover excluded. Signup/billing evidence belongs to provider; downstream abuse alone explicitly insufficient. Existing parent mismatch remains.
Cloud acquisition includes both compromise and provisioning; execution covers provisioning. Resource objective coherent but overlaps two named peers without a mapping boundary.
Purchased premium email resources are coherent, while intro also claims compromise. Payment evidence is differentiated from mail abuse; overlap with establishment/compromise needs policy.

Edited record clearly separates procurement from takeover and later lures/impersonation. Creation/cultivation still overlaps existing FT010.003; document intentional umbrella mapping, without merging identity.

Compromise is a method; Resource Development needs a third-party resource purpose, whereas prose also covers direct victim theft. Login and change telemetry is plausible; regular password-change advice is outdated.
Cloud takeover concept is clear but stolen-payment creation and purchased access are included as compromise examples. These should be mapped distinctly; provider log access is assumed.
Email takeover differs from purchasing already-compromised access; record includes both. Authentication, forwarding and settings changes support compromise where provider/owner telemetry exists.
Edited unauthorized takeover targets existing social account as a trusted resource. Buyer procurement, later impersonation and lures clearly distinguished; visibility and corroboration explicit.
Compromise of third-party infrastructure for later operations is coherent Resource Development; broad Acquire Access peers already cover examples. External-visibility caveat appropriate.
Creating/cultivating resources fits Resource Development; persona use is downstream. Broad Acquire Access overlaps establishment; no identity merger inferred.

Cloud-account creation differs from direct takeover, but FT007.008 duplicates provisioning. Parent semantically FT010, declared FT011 is pre-existing error. External-visibility limitation appropriate.
Email creation differs from takeover; paid creation overlaps acquisition peer. Parent semantic fit FT010, not current FT011. Detection appropriately acknowledges external activity.
Social persona creation/cultivation fits establishment; subsequent impersonation/lures separate. Same creation behavior retained in edited procurement umbrella, requiring documented overlap mapping.

Telegram-account creation is coherent resource preparation; end-to-end encryption is generalized to bot/group C2 despite Telegram cloud/secret-chat distinction. Network use cannot prove account establishment.
Victim merchant-account takeover fits Initial Access, distinguishable from preparing a third-party resource. Login/settings/transaction signals are useful corroborative leads.
API credential use is distinct from prior exposure scanning. All examples chiefly describe exposure, and permissions/key type constrain control; takeover should require evidence of unauthorized use.
Use of leaked login credentials fits takeover; password spraying is a different acquisition mechanism and listed phish is earlier in chain. Signals are plausible, not proof alone.

Stolen bearer sessions can enable Initial Access, distinct from passwords; SameSite/CSRF token-theft claim conflates request forgery with confidentiality. Named malware examples need retained evidence.
Self-service recovery via PII fits ATO but lacks concrete recovery prerequisites, examples and detection. PII alone should not be asserted sufficient across platforms.
Fake-ID recovery can enable takeover, while FT052 is document fabrication. Needs verification/recovery prerequisites and detection; a submitted fake ID does not itself establish access.
Compromised email followed by password reset is a coherent takeover chain; lacks recovery constraints, MFA implications, examples and detection.
XSS-induced redirection is distinct from copied-site creation and in-page skimming; form-action tampering overlaps data theft. Detection field lists prevention only, leaving observability undefined.
Resource Hijacking text repeats account/API-key takeover instead of specifying resource-consumption hijacking. No detection; owner should decide distinct concept or retained alias lineage.

Compromising suppliers/integrations to reach merchant data fits Initial Access; supplier compromise alone does not grant all customers' secrets. Integration/endpoint telemetry depends on supplier access.
Recovery/support workflow abuse coherently specifies the mechanism underlying several ATO children. Correlating support contacts, approvals and access activity is suitable.

Credential/payment/PII lures are coherent, but contrast in FT001 wrongly reserves Initial Access phishing to code execution. Access-seeking versus targeting-information purpose should separate mappings.
Merchant credentials are the target object; email/SMS/social are channels. Explicit subset fits parent; social example can also map FT018 without identity collapse.
PII elicitation intended for recovery fits phishing; claim of resetting 2FA needs workflow prerequisites and detection. Sparse record remains reviewable but incomplete.
Backup-code elicitation fits phishing; code usually replaces one authentication factor rather than universally granting access directly. Password/session prerequisites and detection absent.

Specific scope is malicious advertising leading to skimming, narrower than broad ad fraud. Initial Access is plausible for traffic delivery; compromised-merchant and fake-storefront examples are distinct paths.

Edited access-seeking social lures retain credential and malicious-file branches; public-profile harvesting and downstream harm correctly excluded as defining behavior. Detection distinguishes alternative paths and evidence owners.
Cloning trusted appearance fits deception tactic; harvesting and malware are uses. HTTPS is insufficient to establish site legitimacy and its detection advice risks that inference.

Stolen identity used in merchant onboarding differs from generic fake-business onboarding. Defense evasion plausible as false identity, while resource creation is another lens; no mandatory multi-tactic change inferred.
Edited trusted-identity misrepresentation is distinct from fictional personas, acquisition and phishing. V1 concealment tactic choice defensible; detection checks authorization, not sentiment alone.
Describes rapid stolen-card spending after testing; Defense Evasion placement and 'Churning' terminology lack a clear concealment-specific boundary. Velocity detection is relevant.
All examples describe legitimate complaint resolution; adversarial evasion is not established. Duplicate-name peer repeats this problem and detection recommends the behavior itself.
False/reused tracking to defeat disputes coherently fits evasion; overlaps fabricated shipping child. Carrier/address correlation useful but requires carrier data access.
Fabricated reputation signals fit deception; phishing links are subsequent use. Review timing/text/accounts are leads; verified purchase does not itself authenticate a review.

Parent prose centers financial-statement manipulation while children target onboarding/identity documents. Broad title could contain both, but parent needs explicit scope linkage; accounting detection misses document forgery.
Forged business-registration evidence coherently fits broad falsification title and evasion. Registry corroboration relevant; availability and authorization depend on jurisdiction.
License confers permission versus registration establishing entity; distinction intentional. Document and issuing-authority checks relevant, subject to jurisdiction and access.
VAT registration evidence is a distinct verification object; forged-number/document checks plausible, but country-specific access/acceptance are not validated.

EIN verification-letter forgery is coherent; lawful database-access qualifier helps. Need official nomenclature/source retention and onboarding acceptance evidence, not proof that every processor accepts it.
SS-4 application versus issued EIN confirmation naming is imprecise and risks conflating separate documents; official-source follow-up needed. Corroboration logic is otherwise plausible.

Post-access privilege/capability discovery coheres as internal discovery. Referenced tactic absent; neither pre-target Reconnaissance nor execution automatically resolves intent. UI/API visibility assumed.
Balance/payout reconnaissance fits enumeration parent and differs from exporting reports for theft. API balance reads are plausible; detailed log availability needs deployment evidence.
Feature discovery plausible; claimed Stripe Standard/Pro/Enterprise account-tier structure is unsupported. Specify actual product/account capabilities and APIs before validating examples.
Rule inspection and black-box probing are different discovery routes. Dashboard scope plausible; general rule-list API and hypothetical testing capability need endpoint evidence.

Phishing from a compromised relationship can expand access; customer payment-diversion examples are not necessarily internal lateral movement. Needs boundary for external victims versus internal proliferation.
Cross-account trusted permissions can propagate access, but example equates accountant access with payout-settings authority. Roles are capability-specific; exact preconditions need evidence.

Testing stolen cards by low-value attempts coheres under transactions and differs from monetization. Payment-attempt telemetry useful; account and IP velocities are corroborative, not universal rules.

Legitimate gateway compromise differs from a counterfeit gateway. Merchant checkout tampering examples need a clearer boundary from gateway-infrastructure compromise; provider and merchant visibility differ.
Parent defines digital frontend skimming almost entirely as JavaScript, making child near-duplicate; fake phishing site example changes mechanism. Collection tactic fit also warrants owner review.
Injected JavaScript data capture is coherent, but little contrast remains with parent. Script-integrity and outbound-request evidence relevant; CSP/SRI do not cover all trusted-script compromise.
Buyer avoidance of shipping-address collection is a different actor/behavior from seller non-fulfillment children. This is a substantive hierarchy defect beyond blank parent fields.
Deliberate seller non-delivery is coherent but does not specialize buyer shipping-address evasion. Claimed typical10-to50-dollar price range lacks evidence; complaints/fulfillment mismatch are leads.
Selective fulfillment differs from total non-delivery; first example reverses its rationale by shipping cheap orders then invoking reluctance to dispute cheap items. Parent concept mismatch remains.
Deliberately wrong goods is coherent seller fraud, distinct from never shipping; parent semantics conflict and detection absent. Existing blank-parent/date anomalies remain.
Fabricated shipment status overlaps FT024; delay-versus-dispute emphasis is a possible distinction, not yet a clean boundary. Parent mismatch and missing detection remain.

Three-party stolen-card fulfillment chain is coherent and distinct from no-delivery. Profit is victim customer payment, not necessarily a price spread; shipping/billing mismatch alone is weak evidence.
Description and detection prescribe ordinary service recovery; adversarial transaction manipulation absent. Duplicate name is insufficient justification to merge, but semantic distinction is missing.
Dishonest buyer refund/return claims differ from merchant non-fulfillment. Non-defective returns alone can be legitimate; deception/policy breach must remain the criterion.

Historical FT053 collision repaired and UUID distinct. Specific single-letter-name fail-open claim requires processor/version/issuer evidence; normal fallback is not proof of universal bypass. Detection absent.
Account control/persistence can fit broad V1 C2, but bank/payout examples duplicate cash-out family. Need intent boundary and concrete control-maintenance examples.
Unauthorized added team member supports persistence under V1 C2; audit of membership/roles is relevant. Distinction from Additional Authorized Account is not established.
New users and permissions repeat sibling almost completely; no distinct authorization object is defined. Same detection surface; preserve UUID until owner decides taxonomy.
Text means bank/debit payout destination, while same-named FT042.002 means Stripe account linkage. This is intentional object distinction obscured by names; overlaps FT042.005 directly.

Unauthorized data extraction coherent; claimed direct database access via compromised Stripe account needs support. Most examples are supported types of exports, but exact field visibility is not established.
Revenue data is the target object; reporting route overlaps Sigma/billing analytics and can be multi-mapped. Export anomalies require account audit visibility and authorization context.
Payout-report theft fits parent, but diverting funds is not data exfiltration. Claimed bank-number completeness and export fields require evidence; schedule anomalies may indicate another technique.

Billing/subscription analytics is a coherent data subset, overlapping revenue and Sigma route. Detection assumes account audit access; aggregate metric export differs from exposed full payment credentials.
Sigma query/export abuse is a coherent tool-specific route; generic full-card implications and promised per-query alert/IP-allowlist controls need product evidence.
Generic Data Transfer substantially repeats Data Exfiltration; child pipeline route is specific. Copying data does not itself obscure the originating financial ledger as laundering claim implies.
Unauthorized warehouse sharing is coherent; declared parent FT038 differs from intended FT039. Automatic sharing is not deletion of source financial history; laundering inference unsupported.

Carding-market trade is resource procurement/sale, but all examples/detection mainly cover subsequent card testing/spending. Cash-out placement requires seller monetization or explicit chain boundary.
Abuse of shell entities to disguise transactions fits laundering; shell status alone does not establish fraud. Corporate and flow verification should corroborate actual abusive activity.
Cash-out intent distinguishes from persistence in principle, but broad prose includes unauthorized access and repeats FT037. Mapping convention needed; UUIDs must remain distinct meanwhile.
Added consumer payment instruments differ from merchant payout destinations, but description mixes both. Monitoring added instruments useful with ownership and transaction context.
Other Stripe-account linkage differs from bank destinations despite identical title. Generic linking does not automatically confer balances/authority; specify Connect/organization/trust mechanism.
BNPL enablement may be abused, but merchant-controlled credit terms/delayed merchant payment assertions conflict with provider-funded BNPL. Detection targets settings that may not exist.
Payout schedule manipulation is coherent but duplicates Scheduled Payout; adding independent schedules/destinations requires product-specific evidence. Schedule and destination are distinct settings.
Unauthorized bank destination addition fits cash-out; same concrete behavior exists in C2 sibling. Authorization and configuration logs relevant; do not assume bank addition alone guarantees payout.
Unauthorized Connect child creation fits cash-out preparation, but detection is copied from feature enablement and omits creation/ownership/destination events.

Unauthorized feature enablement coherent in principle; transaction-limit and international-toggle examples require actual product permissions and provider controls. Account/API visibility not universal.
Unauthorized funding-source top-up is coherent cash-out preparation; promotional credits/balance inflation claims need support. Distinguish moving real funds from creating artificial balance.

Recurring unauthorized funds transfer is coherent; Stripe transfer versus bank payout semantics need explicit destination/object boundary. Reporting-threshold evasion is a scenario, not a universal threshold.
Timing cash-out through payout settings fits tactic but overlaps schedule-manipulation child. Need product-supported multi-schedule semantics and destination constraints.

Distributed traffic disruption fits Impact; provider/network visibility required. Target descriptions are hypothetical scenarios, not claims of observed Stripe incidents; legal-reporting generalization unvalidated.
Single-source service exhaustion is distinguishable from distributed floods, but DoS is broader than flooding. Availability/traffic evidence coherent where infrastructure telemetry exists.
Deleting account/control artifacts to hinder inquiry fits evidence concealment intent; merchant ability to delete Stripe security logs or all traces is unproven. Preserve provider-retention limits.
Locking out legitimate owners fits persistence/control or disruption more directly than destruction of evidence. Evidence-obstruction intent possible but removal itself does not erase audit logs.

Fraudulent merchant onboarding fits platform entry; stolen identity is one variant, not required. Resource Development is another plausible objective; V1 choice requires consistent mapping, not silent reclassification.
Conversion to cash coherent, but ordinary online card fields do not establish usable magnetic-stripe track data/PIN for ATM cloning. Specify prerequisites and separate card-present from resale route.
Stolen-payment purchasing for resale/cash-out coherent, while purchases for personal use/resource building are broader than laundering. Transaction signals do not prove subsequent monetization.

Subscription resale can monetize theft; recurring purchase of legitimate services alone is not a specified laundering chain. 'Subscription stuffing' also conflates credential testing with procurement.
Buying SMS capacity can be resource development; alleged laundering/reshipping route lacks a coherent digital-service-to-proceeds mechanism. Provider payment evidence supports procurement only.

Title says LLM Services but all prose/detection concerns language-learning materials. Intended concept must be decided before any rewrite; preserving current UUID does not settle replacement identity.
Nitro/gift resale is a plausible monetization route; merely gifting or using services does not prove funds laundering. Platform/payment-provider data required for transaction correlations.

Identity-document fabrication fits evasion; document, holder-binding and onboarding outcomes are separate checks. Generic global databases/AI/metadata claims require explicit coverage and failure limits.
Passport booklet forgery is distinct from passport card; flat images cannot demonstrate genuine optical/UV features. Biometric face match is holder comparison, not proof identity document is genuine.
Driver license is distinct from non-driver state ID, although attack mechanism shared. Claimed global verification and metadata/AI certainty need qualification and supported jurisdiction scope.
National-card forgery fits parent; jurisdiction-specific document types distinct from US state cards. Database access, image features and platform acceptance require evidence.
US visa-card nomenclature and acceptance are ambiguous relative to visa foil/BCC/green card. Preserve separate ID pending owner decision; document claims need official examples.
Municipal NYC identity card is a distinct issuer object; actual Stripe acceptance and database access are not established. Detection generic rather than issuer-specific.
BCC is a specific identity/travel object; distinction from generic US visa-card entry needs documented issuer scope. Verification-access and feature-observation limitations remain.
Residence permit/green card forgery coherent but groups jurisdictions/document families. Generic image, holder-match and registry checks need explicit limits and platform acceptance scope.
Passport-card description is distinct, but entire detection section instead names resident permits/green cards. Confirmed copied-object defect alongside generic evidence limitations.
State ID description is coherent, but entire detection section instead names resident permits/green cards. Distinguish non-driver ID from license and correct object-specific guidance separately.
Payment-data elicitation coherent, but Collection tactic seems closer than transaction manipulation and parent overlaps Card Details child. Detection missing; distinct UUID from3DS preserved.
Billing Information includes card number/CVV/expiry, making sibling Card Details substantially duplicate. Need billing-address versus instrument-fields boundary; no detection provided.
Shipping contact collection is a distinct information object but need not collect a cardholder's card data. Broad parent can contain it if intent explicit; no detection provided.
Instrument-data collection via lures/malware is coherent; overlaps billing sibling and digital skimming route. Online fields alone insufficient for magnetic-stripe cloning; detection missing.
Fraud storefront presentation differs from merchant-account onboarding and fulfillment fraud, though they chain. Cloning is an optional route; no detection provided.
Counterfeit payment interface differs from compromising genuine gateway. Credential/card capture is downstream objective; no detection provided.

Target information collection is coherent and all16 assigned techniques broadly concern discovery before access. Purchasing stolen credentials overlaps Resource Development; FT027 is post-access discovery and has no matching tactic, so do not force it here.

Resource preparation definition is coherent, including infrastructure and collaborators.21 assigned rows include direct victim intrusion and creation/takeover mixtures; define purpose of prepared resource. Mule/recruitment examples without dedicated techniques are coverage opportunities, not automatically defects.

Unauthorized foothold/access objective coherent.18 assigned rows include fraudulent onboarding and ads; account-entry lens can explain these, but consistency with Resource Development requires convention. No automatic V2 backport.

Definition includes running code and unauthorized transactions; no techniques currently reference Execution. Overlap with Manipulation & Fraudulent Transactions is real but an unused tactic alone does not prove a defect; owner should decide scope/coverage.

Legitimacy concealment and evading detection are coherent, supporting edited impersonation placement.25 assigned rows include rapid spending and benign dispute handling needing follow-up. Timing/objective distinguishes post-fraud evidence destruction, not an exclusive partition.

Expansion from an existing foothold is coherent. Cross-account trusted access fits; external customer payment phishing is not necessarily internal proliferation. Two assigned records reviewed; no observed-incident claim inferred.

Unauthorized transactions/manipulation coherent;17 assigned rows also contain collection-only behavior and legitimate service. Need objective mapping for skimming/cardholder collection and remove unsupported fraud assumptions; not a mandate to recategorize all today.

Definition explicitly includes persistent backdoor access and remote financial actions, making user-account persistence defensible in V1. Bank-destination linkage alone is cash-out rather than a control channel. Four assigned records reviewed; do not impose ATT&CK label semantics automatically.

Collection/extraction objective coherent; seven assigned rows cover reports and warehouse transfers, but network-only wording understates hosted data and elicited information. FT053/FT032 provide a tactic-boundary question, not proof a missing new tactic is required.

Post-fraud concealment and monetization definition coherent, but19 assigned rows include earlier resource procurement and unsupported laundering inferences. Cash-out does not automatically establish laundering, and shell entities alone are not unlawful.

Availability/reputation disruption and distraction objective coherent. Two assigned DoS variants differ by distributed source. No independent reputation-manipulation technique is present; that is a coverage opportunity subject to evidence and scope.

Post-fraud investigation obstruction is coherent and distinguishable by evidence object/purpose. Account deletion may obstruct visibility but need not erase provider records; owner lockout often serves persistence/impact. Two assigned rows reviewed.
